learning: Iteration 4 showed that 20 mm pitch with a 0.10 m track and 0.6 kg mass cut slalom progress to 0.035 and did not move s-bend progress off 0.04. Compare this race with iteration 2: the only geometry change is the forward offset. If s-bend progress stays at 0.04, forward lead is not the lever and the next test should be a larger lead or a different drivetrain change.
notes: Adopts the Builder's iteration 5 geometry (16 mm contiguous at ±0.048 m, y = 0.05 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg) with the iteration 2 controller unchanged. This isolates forward sensor lead against the iteration 2 and 3 baseline.
rationale: Iteration 4 cut slalom progress from 0.104 to 0.035 and left s-bend progress at 0.04, so the 20 mm pitch and the 0.10 m track / 0.6 kg mass combination did not help. Iteration 3 showed kp 5.0 vs 5.0 gives identical s-bend results, so gain is not the lever. The s-bend has zero line loss and ends at max_error about 0.061 m, which points to the sensors reaching the bend too late. I therefore adopt the Builder's iteration 5 geometry exactly: contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m, forward offset y = 0.05 m, wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.8 kg (the iteration 2 values with the best oval and slalom progress). Controller is held at the iteration 2 and 3 values (kp 5.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.5, last_direction line loss) so the race isolates forward lead. Weights stay proportional to x, so a positive signal steers left as the contract requires. Expected: s-bend progress above 0.04, slalom progress near 0.104, and no oval line loss. These are predictions, not measured results.
